assumptions: DORA register obligations and regulator validation requirements remain materially similar over the proposed commercialization period.
At least some outsourced compliance or audit operators manage enough regulated entities to make a portfolio-level contract operationally meaningful.
The proposed benchmark can use representative multilingual registers without violating client confidentiality or data-protection obligations.
Specialist regulatory review, security controls, insurance, and contractual liability limits can be obtained within the stated capital and part-time operating constraints.
The proposed prices are gross revenue before any partner revenue share, specialist review cost, onboarding effort, or liability-related expense.
No traction, partner commitment, reusable correction corpus, performance advantage, or approved data rights exist beyond the evidence stated in the packet.
evidence_needed_for_higher_score: A signed 12-month multi-entity partner minimum; a representative blinded benchmark showing materially better regulator-format pass rate and repair time than the partner's current process and named incumbents; measured human-review minutes, onboarding cost, gross margin, and partner-level CAC payback; documented security, liability, and cross-tenant data-rights acceptance; and evidence that register changes and annual cycles create enough repeat usage and renewal value.

factors.name: Core insight
factors.rationale: The concept identifies a real control point between a partner's preparation workflow and regulatory submission, and narrows the product to evidence-linked exception repair rather than another system of record. The insight is coherent and supported by failure data, but it is not yet established that this narrow layer is a distinct purchasable category rather than a feature of existing tools or services.

factors.name: Customer pain and willingness to pay
factors.rationale: The 6.5% dry-run pass rate and Polish resubmission stage directly support consequential preparation and repair pain under deadlines. However, they do not establish durable willingness to pay for a separate repair layer, and free official materials, internal teams, partner workflows, and bundled incumbent products are credible substitutes. Recurring error volume after early filing cycles is unknown.

factors.name: Business model and economics
factors.rationale: An annual portfolio minimum plus per-entity use could produce recurring, high-margin revenue with low capital exposure if integrations and human review stay bounded. All decisive economics remain hypothetical: partner share, sales cycle, onboarding cost, exception labor, renewal, liability expense, and CAC payback are unmeasured. The proposed per-entity realization also competes with transparent prices for broader incumbent products, while the founder-wealth path requires 600 covered entities and EU-scale retention.

factors.name: Market and beachhead
factors.rationale: Outsourced DORA compliance and audit operators are a precise beachhead with portfolio leverage and a clear trigger. The reachable operator count, portfolio sizes, unserved entity base, budgets, and procurement cadence are unknown, so there is no evidence that this narrow segment alone supports the required scale. The illustrated outcome appears to depend on substantial EU expansion.

factors.name: Competitive position and domination potential
factors.rationale: White-label embedding and focus on repair may reduce direct system-of-record competition, but DAPR is an exact local incumbent and Vendorica and ReportAct already cover overlapping extraction, reconciliation, validation, and export workflows. Partners can also retain spreadsheets or internal tooling. No exclusive channel, performance proof, switching barrier, or protected control point currently supports domination.

factors.name: Expansion potential
factors.rationale: A successful partner deployment could extend across that operator's client portfolio, additional EU geographies, languages, and ongoing register changes. The same validation architecture might later support adjacent regulated submissions, but that adjacency is not specified or evidenced and would add domain and integration burden. Expansion is plausible but not yet structurally unlocked.

factors.name: Defensibility and durability
factors.rationale: Versioned regression tests, evidence-linked audit trails, workflow integration, and an outcomes corpus could compound. Yet reusable data rights are unresolved, tenant-local learning may not compound, and incumbents can add a repair queue using their installed data and customer relationships. No corpus, exclusive partner agreement, or measured learning advantage exists today.

factors.name: Strength of advantage
factors.rationale: Requesting only evidence excerpts, fitting existing files, and returning an auditable repair package could reduce custody, review time, and switching friction. Those benefits have not been measured against partners' current processes or the broader capabilities of named competitors, so there is no demonstrated step-change in price, accuracy, speed, or risk.

factors.name: Timing and momentum
factors.rationale: DORA is binding, structured reporting is recent, and official failure and resubmission evidence creates a timely opening while workflows are still forming. Counterbalancing this, capable vendors are already in market and error-driven demand may fall as entities and advisers learn the process. Timing is favorable for a benchmark, not proof of a durable business.

factors.name: Distribution
factors.rationale: Selling to portfolio operators can turn one relationship into many covered entities and fits the founder better than direct regulated-entity sales. The paid benchmark and minimum-volume gate are disciplined acquisition mechanisms. Still, no partner has accepted them, and these sophisticated, trust-sensitive buyers may prefer internal workflows, incumbents, or ownership of the remediation process; procurement length and repeatability are unknown.

factors.name: Execution and risks
factors.rationale: The deterministic QA core and measurement harness fit the founder's technical skills, the staged capital requirement is affordable, and AI can accelerate development. Reliable regulatory interpretation, multilingual extraction, security, daytime enterprise procurement, specialist review, insurance, and error liability cannot be automated away and may exceed a part-time founder's capacity. A false repair has material downstream consequences.

highest_value_structural_change: Move the control point upstream from episodic filing repair to a continuous operator-side acceptance gate for every new or changed ICT contract, while retaining official register preflight as the measurable output. Contracting for embedded use across the partner's whole portfolio would create more frequent paid events, deeper workflow switching costs, and a better correction corpus; this change should be pursued only if a partner benchmark proves it does not recreate a costly system of record.
main_structural_strength: A single embedded operator relationship can aggregate many regulated entities, while the paid benchmark and minimum-volume condition prevent a speculative production build and make superior pass rate or repair time the commercial proof point.
primary_score_limiter: There is no evidence that operators will pay the proposed minimum for a narrow repair layer often enough to sustain attractive economics, nor that its performance or defensibility exceeds existing full-register products and internal workflows.
strongest_disconfirming_evidence: A Warsaw-based exact incumbent already sells automated validation and full-register functionality for EUR 2,000-8,000 annually, Vendorica and ReportAct offer overlapping recurring products, and official forms remain free; this makes the proposed 5,000-7,000 PLN per-entity repair economics and durable differentiation particularly uncertain.
